## Deploy readiness board (R100, informational)

This check is informational on pull requests during the pre-launch
burn-down. It gates only the codebase-invariant sections (stub values
and prod-switch coherence). The environment-dependent sections (wiring,
env discovery, operator keys) are surfaced below but do not block the
PR because the runner carries no production secrets. The prod-deploy
gate (deploy-readiness-gate) enforces every section under strict mode.


AUDIT GPT-6.1 Sol — growth-project-backend#673 @ df76889fb862095170498dccb23f35db3d116690 — VERDICT: REQUEST CHANGES

A/B/C = 0/1/2

Reviewer: agent 118, job AUD-SOL-T23-118; independent first full T4 audit of this 11-file / 2,627-line T3 piece, including original #656 history, all restacks, the round-8 trial-end writer, checkout/billing call sites, transaction/post-commit boundaries, conflict retry/alert worker and every piece test. [Candidate and round 8](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/673#issuecomment-5977778572)

### Prior findings first

**Original B-656-1 closes at its reported ephemeral-obligation boundary:** a lost one-trial race durably owes cancellation in the webhook transaction, process loss/transient failure leaves replayable work, and later trialing/$0-invoice events retain the access veto; the candidate lifecycle controls pass, but destructive retries after an already-paid conversion expose the additional boundary below. [Original finding](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/656#issuecomment-5965268813) [Current candidate controls](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37218265800)

**B-656-6 closes at its reported shared-alert-receipt boundary:** `billed_alerted_at` is separate from `alerted_at`, and a failed-cancellation alert followed by a processed active conversion still emits the billed alert once, including concurrent alert-sweep controls. [Original finding](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/656#issuecomment-5972091723) [Worker receipts](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/df76889fb862095170498dccb23f35db3d116690/src/packages/trials/trial-conflict.service.ts#L282-L314) [Executed controls](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37218265800)

**B-656-7 closes for T3's direct worker/handler diagnostic changes:** closed classifications remain in the cancellation, alert and settle-lookup paths, and candidate canaries pass; unrelated historical logging is not claimed fixed here. [Current direct diagnostics](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/df76889fb862095170498dccb23f35db3d116690/src/packages/trials/trial-conflict.service.ts) [Executed canaries](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37218265800)

The round-8 C-671-4 writer change preserves `trial_ends_at=null` for never-started attempts and retains started-trial history through cancellation; verified builder before **1 failed / 68 passed**, after **286/286** plus type-check, and current real-handler controls pass. [Writer change and boundary](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/673#issuecomment-5977778572) [Before](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37185687036) [After](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37185762015) [Independent controls](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37218265800)

No approved-code evidence is reused: original #656 had no Sol APPROVE and this piece had no previous Sol verdict; the full current T3 diff was read rather than treating its restack label as inherited approval. [Original Sol verdict](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/656#issuecomment-5972091723) [Piece history](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/673)

### B-673-1 — an owed retry blindly cancels an already-paid plan when the active webhook is delayed/missing

**File:line:** `src/packages/trials/trial-conflict.service.ts:164–225,265–287`; the retry consults only local `status='owed'` and sends `cancelSubscription()` without reconciling Stripe's current billing/subscription state, then writes `cancelled`; the only paid-plan supersession path is triggered by a processed `status='active'` webhook in `checkout-webhook-handler.service.ts:959–976`. [Destructive retry](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/df76889fb862095170498dccb23f35db3d116690/src/packages/trials/trial-conflict.service.ts#L164-L225) [Sweep and alert admission](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/df76889fb862095170498dccb23f35db3d116690/src/packages/trials/trial-conflict.service.ts#L265-L287) [Webhook-only supersession](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/df76889fb862095170498dccb23f35db3d116690/src/checkout/checkout-webhook-handler.service.ts#L959-L976)

**Executed counterexample:** after three cancellation failures spanning the trial end, the local row remains owed while the modeled Stripe subscription is now paid/active and its active webhook has not arrived; the **real TrialConflictService and real StripeConnectApiService**, over an intercepted synthetic fetch, issue **only `DELETE /subscriptions/sub-paid`**, no canonical-state read, and settle the conflict as cancelled. [Exact-source paid-retry failure](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37218424769)

This bypasses the piece's explicit paid-plan policy: an already-billed client is meant to retain the regular paid plan and generate the separate refund/support alert, whereas `cancelled` is excluded from that billed-alert sweep and the subsequent subscription-deleted handler revokes access. [Intended policy and alert selection](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/df76889fb862095170498dccb23f35db3d116690/src/packages/trials/trial-conflict.service.ts#L30-L40) [Actual billed-alert selection](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/df76889fb862095170498dccb23f35db3d116690/src/packages/trials/trial-conflict.service.ts#L282-L287) [Deletion entitlement transition](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/df76889fb862095170498dccb23f35db3d116690/src/checkout/checkout-webhook-handler.service.ts#L1091-L1135)

**Minimal fix rule:** an owed row is not proof that the remote subscription is still a free trial; reconcile authoritative current billing/subscription state before destructive retry, fail closed on unknown state, and durably supersede/arm the billed alert instead of cancelling an already-paid conversion. Fence the state transition/admission so webhook supersession or terminal changes cannot be undone by a stale worker.

**Verification:** retain the paid-active/missed-webhook counterexample; cover trial-end crossing during preparation, active-event-before/after retry, unknown canonical reads, cancellation/deletion, and the unchanged “still trialing -> cancel once” and failure-alert -> billed-alert controls.

### C-673-1 — integrated recurring/trials candidate qualification retained

`src/checkout/checkout.module.ts:49–83` and the trial webhook seam still require the C-656-1/#680 integration list: shared trial schema, one reservation/release authority, capability registration, typed trial parameters and unified webhook state, plus mobile #338 and the configured trial-ending event before deploy. [Integration list and landing contract](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/673#issuecomment-5977778572) [Module seam](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/df76889fb862095170498dccb23f35db3d116690/src/checkout/checkout.module.ts#L49-L83)

That is not a second standalone T3 blocker or approval of real native checkout; T2's separately reported B-672-3 belongs to its owner and is not double-counted against this piece. [T2 exact-head verdict](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/672#issuecomment-5982319373)

### C-673-2 — a late sweep row gets an already-expired cancellation lease

**File:line:** `trial-conflict.service.ts:164–181,220,265–272`; the sweep's single old `now` supplies every serial lease/backoff timestamp, unlike the fresh-clock notice worker. [Lease/backoff](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/df76889fb862095170498dccb23f35db3d116690/src/packages/trials/trial-conflict.service.ts#L164-L220) [Sweep clock](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/df76889fb862095170498dccb23f35db3d116690/src/packages/trials/trial-conflict.service.ts#L265-L272)

**Executed counterexample:** seven prior nine-second cancels (below the real API's ten-second and worker's twenty-second bounds) make the eighth operation start at +63 seconds with a lease ending at +60; a fresh replica five seconds later issues a **second cancellation**, returning `cancelled` instead of `busy`. [Initial execution](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37218265800) [Independent refinement](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37218424769)

The duplicate DELETE alone has not demonstrated a double charge or incorrect final row, because completion fencing remains effective, so it is nonblocking rather than promoted by label; use fresh per-claim/admission/backoff clocks and retain this probe when editing the same B-673-1 admission lines. [Executed result](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37218424769)

### Evidence and CI boundaries

The first test-only child `8fe53f9e418eca8b2f06058b6e065417509e79fa`, directly based on this head, executes **3 deliberate failures / 133 passing controls** across eight targeted suites; two failures belong to T2 and one is C-673-2, with all candidate trial/HTTP/alert controls passing. [First one-job run](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37218265800)

Refined test child `67469107c9f77cef1c845fe80a7d5fd7e3304a3c` preserves every candidate source/schema/dependency input, and workflow receipt `5ccf372a511988309bbabfbf925af17472ddece5` executes **two behavioral failures**—B-673-1 and C-673-2—with no fixture/type failure counted as defect evidence. [Paid-retry refinement](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37218424769)

Applicable stacked candidate checks are green; main-only CodeQL/danger/banned-casts/SBOM remain landing gates, and deploy-readiness skips by policy; this **2,627-line** piece stays below the hard cap. [Candidate CI](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37186105856) [Size/check contract](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/673#issuecomment-5977778572)

Outside-diff never-billed-trial MRR/churn observations are routed only in the operator report, not made blockers on this piece; no candidate-branch edits, local heavy execution, merge, production action or real provider/customer operation. Notes/probes/logs and handoff: `ops/aud-118/AUD-SOL-T23-118/`, `ops/reports/AUD-SOL-T23-118.md`.

AUDIT Claude Opus 5.5 — growth-project-backend#673 @ df76889fb862095170498dccb23f35db3d116690 — VERDICT: APPROVE
A/B/C = 0/0/3

Job AUD-OPUS-T23-118 (agent 118). Tier T4 (money path). Trials T3: webhook trial lifecycle, one trial per client per coach, durable conflict cancel, and the trial view in the purchase list. Base T2 #672 `c5e7ed8e35f1e5b88653e5605dded2af8614182d`. Size: 11 files, +2,619 / -8 = 2,627 changed lines (about 700 source lines), under the 3,000 cap. CI at this head: 10 checks pass, deploy-readiness-gate skipped ([CI run 37186105856](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37186105856)). CodeQL, danger, banned-casts and SBOM run only once this piece is based on main.

### Evidence reuse decision

Nothing reused. This lens never approved #656 or any #673 head, so this is a full fresh audit. Every changed line was read:
- `checkout-webhook-handler.service.ts`: `subscriptionGrantsEntitlement`, `applyTrialState` / `trialTransition`, `applyTrialWillEnd`, `applyInvoicePaid`, `applySubscriptionDeleted`, `deliverTrialNotice` and `cancelTrialConflict`.
- `billing.service.ts`: the event case and the post-commit hooks.
- `trial-conflict.service.ts` (full file), `checkout.service.ts` `listForClient`, `client-purchases.select.ts`, `checkout.module.ts`, `docs/stripe-setup.md` and `.env.example`.
- All three specs, including the round-8 test adjustments (`45100490..df07fabc`), which adapt the tests to T2's stamped-zone and same-process rules without weakening any assertion.

### Prior findings of this lens

**C-671-4 (from #671) is closed at the writer. The builder's claim is accepted on evidence.**
- On this stack the only writer of `ClientPurchase.trial_ends_at` is `checkout-webhook-handler.service.ts:934`. The other `trial_ends_at` writes in `trial-usage.service.ts` are on the `PackageTrialUsage` ledger.
- That writer runs only when the purchase already has an end, when the subscription is `trialing` and entitled, or when the ledger says the trial started (`:930-933`). A lost race returns before the write (`:929`).
- Composed controls through the real handler are green:
  - a $0 trial invoice without a card, then `customer.subscription.deleted`, leaves `trial_ends_at` null and reads `setup_incomplete`, then `none`;
  - a lost race (card saved, trial already used with the same coach), then cancel, leaves `trial_ends_at` null and reads `none`.
  - Evidence: [probe run 37219356220](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37219356220). The PR's own test is `test/b-trials-notice-and-webhook.spec.ts:480`.
- So T1's comment at `trial-view.ts:98-101` now holds. ### C-673-1 — post-commit trial work is awaited inside the webhook request

- **File:line:** `src/billing/billing.service.ts:674-686`. `deliverTrialNotice` (push 30 s + 5 s grace, then email 30 s + 5 s) and `cancelTrialConflict` (20 s deadline) run before the response, so the worst case is about 90 s.
- **Why C:** the [Stripe webhook docs](https://docs.stripe.com/webhooks) say the endpoint must return a 2xx quickly before complex logic. A late reply only causes a retry, which the processed-event dedup absorbs, and both jobs are idempotent with a 5-minute sweep as backstop.
- **Minimal fix rule:** start both post-commit jobs without awaiting them (`void ... .catch(log)`), and leave retries to the sweeps.

### C-673-2 — an older subscription event rewrites an extended trial end

- **File:line:** `checkout-webhook-handler.service.ts:930-934`. Once a purchase has a trial end, `!!purchase.trial_ends_at` writes whatever `trial_end` the event carries, with no ordering check.
- **Counterexample (probe, red as expected):** the trial was extended to +9 d. A pre-extension `customer.subscription.updated` (+2 d) is retried late. The purchase goes back to +2 d, and `recordIfDue` records a notice for the old date. The view and the notice then name a day before the real charge. Evidence: [probe run 37219356220](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37219356220).
- **Why C:** it needs a Stripe-side trial edit, which no product path makes, plus a late retry of the earlier event. The wrong date is earlier than the charge, which is the safe direction for money. The same ordering gap for `status` is pre-existing recurring code, so it goes to the report.
- **Minimal fix rule:** write `trial_ends_at` only from the newest subscription state. Either re-read the subscription before applying trial fields on `customer.subscription.updated`, or skip an event whose `created` is older than the last one applied to the purchase.

### C-673-3 — outside this diff: coach metrics count never-billed trials (binding ruling)

- **File:line:** `src/coach-connect/coach-connect.service.ts:281-295` (MRR from `entitlement_active` recurring purchases), `:307-314` (`clients_churned_30d` counts every `canceled` purchase) and `:339-346` (sub-coach churn, same rule).
